subject: KPI runway health: owners & shortfall remediation
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: KPI runway health: owners & shortfall remediation

Team —

Quick summary for QBR prep: leadership asked for a concise "runway health" readout (latency/cost/uptime/usage) and an owners matrix for remediation. I pulled the 30‑day dashboard overnight and flagged three shortfalls we need to cover in the QBR deck: 

- Latency: 95th tail latency (text-gen P99/95 mix) is up ~18% vs prior month on peak windows; correlates with increased long‑context requests from a small number of customers.
- Cost: cost per productive token has risen ~14% (billing window); prelim signal points to suboptimal batching + L2 cache churn.
- Uptime: two small cluster incidents last week contributed to a 0.12% availability dip on eu-west-1.
- Usage: active seat count and request volume are still growing (+22% M/M) which is masking the efficiency regressions.

Attachments: kpi_runway_heatmap_v3.png (visual heatmap), uptime-delta-table.csv (incident slices). Drive deck link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/QBR/2026-Nov-KPI-Runway

Action needed by EOD today so I can fold into the draft QBR slides: please reply with a one-line owner assignment for each shortfall (Latency / Cost / Uptime) + estimated mitigation ETA (48h, 7d, 30d). If you have a short supporting artifact (small table or ticket), attach or paste.

Proposed quick sync at 11:00 PT if we need to debate priorities — otherwise I will consolidate assignees and circulate the slide.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Ops | Redwood Inference

Quick notes:
- I'll open INF-8272 to capture the latency deep dive (root cause: long‑context KV cache pressure + a small percent of outlier requests that bypass caching).
- Need request samples (top 10 hashes) and the tail‑latency traces from 11/3 and 11/5; Laura, can you confirm those logs are in the shared bucket?

ETA: initial triage and prioritized action list by 7d (2026-11-14) with a 48h short‑term mitigation proposal (cache-tune + config tweak) by 2026-11-09.

I'll own Cost.

Notes:
- Preliminary look suggests batching inefficiencies at our shard-level queue and higher cold-start/eviction churn in the L2 cache for long-context jobs. If we increase max batch latency from 12ms -> 18ms for low-priority routes and enable the new adaptive batching knob in staging, we expect a ~9-11% drop in cost/unit on the tested traffic mix.
- I'll attach a short table (uptake vs cost) and a runbook snippet in qbr-prep-notes.docx.
- Jonas: logs are in s3://redwood-prod-logs/kpi-samples/ — I uploaded the 11/03 + 11/05 tail traces you asked for (samples_20261103.json, samples_20261105.json).

ETA: enable adaptive batching in canary by 2026-11-09; full rollout conditionally by 2026-11-16 after ROI monitor for token-economics.

For Acme Analytics specifically (cc'd below for transparency) I recommend we proactively offer a post‑mortem and a temporary routing exception to their dedicated pool while we stabilize.

- Remove the canary traffic slice from the eu-west-1 rollout for 24h (ops to confirm).
